q: The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is uniform. Do not trade uniform for non-uniform or zero.

q: The relation between potential difference $V$ and electric field intensity $E$ between two parallel plates separated by distance $d$ is $V = $ _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The relation between potential difference V and electric field intensity E between two parallel plates separated by distance d is V = Ed. Do not trade Ed for rac{E}{d} or rac{d}{E}.

q: According to the equation $V = Ed$, the unit of electric field intensity can also be expressed as volt per _____ ($ ext{V m}^{-1}$).
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. According to the equation V = Ed, the unit of electric field intensity can also be expressed as volt per metre ( ext{V m}^-1). Do not trade metre for second or coulomb.

q: Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of same size and same material, carrying charges of equal magnitude and _____ signs.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of same size and same material, carrying charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs. Do not trade opposite for same or neutral.

q: The work done in bringing a unit positive charge from the negative plate to the positive plate against the electric force is $W = $ _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done in bringing a unit positive charge from the negative plate to the positive plate against the electric force is W = Ed. Rac{e}{d} or eq is not this quantity.

q: The units $ ext{V m}^{-1}$ and _____ for the electric field intensity are indeed equivalent.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The units ext{V m}^-1 and ext{N C}^-1 for the electric field intensity are indeed equivalent. Ext{j c}^-1 or ext{w m}^-1 is not this quantity.

q: The distance between two parallel charged plates A and B is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The distance between two parallel charged plates A and B is represented by the symbol d. R or x is not this quantity.

q: The electric field intensity between parallel plates is $E = $ _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field intensity between parallel plates is E = rac{V}{d}. Vd or rac{d}{v} is not this quantity.

q: Parallel charged plates carry charges of equal _____ and opposite signs.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Parallel charged plates carry charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs. Volume or density is not this quantity.

q: In a uniform electric field between parallel plates, the electric field intensity $E$ is _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. In a uniform electric field between parallel plates, the electric field intensity E is constant. Do not trade constant for variable or zero.

q: The work done in carrying an electron from one plate to another is equal to the _____ of the electron when it strikes the plate.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done in carrying an electron from one plate to another is equal to the kinetic energy of the electron when it strikes the plate. Do not trade kinetic energy for potential energy or rest mass.

q: The electric potential difference between two parallel charged plates is the work done in bringing a _____ charge from one plate to another.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential difference between two parallel charged plates is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one plate to another. Do not trade unit positive for unit negative or neutral.

q: If the distance between two parallel plates is doubled while keeping the potential difference constant, the electric field intensity becomes _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. If the distance between two parallel plates is doubled while keeping the potential difference constant, the electric field intensity becomes halved. Doubled or unchanged is not this quantity.

q: The direction of the electric field between two parallel charged plates is from the _____ plate to the _____ plate.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The direction of the electric field between two parallel charged plates is from the positive, negative plate to the _____ plate. Negative, positive or neutral, positive is not this quantity.
